definitions.title: L'Hôpital's Rule for 0/0 and inf/inf
definitions.statement: Suppose f and g are differentiable near c (except possibly at c) and g'(x) != 0 near c. If lim_{x->c} f(x)/g(x) produces an indeterminate form 0/0 or inf/inf, then the limit equals lim_{x->c} f'(x)/g'(x), provided this limit exists or is infinite.
conditions: Differentiate numerator and denominator separately (do NOT use quotient rule!)
definitions.explanation: Derived rigorously from Cauchy's Mean Value Theorem: [f(x) - f(c)]/[g(x) - g(c)] = f'(xi)/g'(xi).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Differentiate top and bottom separately ONLY when indeterminate 0/0 or inf/inf.

definitions.title: Logarithmic Transformation for Indeterminate Powers
definitions.latex: y = [f(x)]^{g(x)} \implies \ln y = g(x) \ln[f(x)], \quad \lim y = e^{\lim \ln y}
definitions.statement: Indeterminate powers of the forms 0^0, oo^0, and 1^oo are evaluated by taking the natural logarithm, converting the exponent into a product g(x)*ln(f(x)), evaluating that limit L, and taking e^L.
definitions.explanation: Transforms indeterminate powers into 0*oo, which in turn becomes 0/0 or inf/inf.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Use natural logarithms to pull down the exponent for 0^0, inf^0, and 1^inf.
